title: Fastlane release debrief and canary tuning playbook
body:
OVERVIEW:
This is a compact fastlane checklist and debrief template for 48-hour micro-releases where we prefer a nimble canary + rapid rollback strategy. Objective: land low-risk changes to the serving runtime and routing logic with clear telemetry gates and an explicit rollback matrix. Use this doc as the day-of runbook and then append debrief notes for the release digest.

SCOPE:
- Target: serving-runtime v2.11.3 (hotfix: kv-cache fence and retry backoff tuning)
- Affects: Hosted API and Dedicated pools only (no Private VPC changes)
- Traffic window: non-peak APAC -> global ramp if green

TIMELINE (compact calendar):
- T-48h: Draft release notes + PRs merged to candidate branch. Notify #release-orbit and product owners.
- T-24h: Preflight smoke on staging: kv-cache replay test, backpressure sim, cold-start latency table. Confirm perf numbers in telemetry.
- T-12h: Canary config baked: traffic split 1% -> 5% -> 20% if thresholds pass. Canary cohort pinned to single AZ.
- T-4h: All hands triage window: SRE, runtime, infra on-call. Final runbook review.
- T-0h: Canary rollout start. Start 1% for 30m.
- T+30m: Evaluate canary metrics; if green move to 5% for 45m.
- T+2h: Evaluate, move to 20% for 2h. If stable, schedule global 100% full roll for low-traffic window or progressive across regions.
- T+24h: Post-launch debrief + tagging for postmortem artifacts.

PREFLIGHT CHECKLIST (must pass before T-12h):
- [ ] All PRs merged and CI green (link in linked_artifacts).
- [ ] Canary AMI/containers built and pushed to registry.
- [ ] Healthcheck endpoints validated (smoke results attached).
- [ ] Telemetry dashboards: canary-latency, canary-error-rate, kv-cache-hit, retry-rate created and bookmarked.
- [ ] Alert overrides prepared (mute noisy non-actionable alerts for rollout).
- [ ] Run synthetic prompt set (10 prompts, 5 seeds) against candidate; quality regression < 0.5% on eval metrics.
- [ ] Rollback play documented and rollback artifacts (previous image tags) staged.

CANARY TUNING PARAMETERS (defaults for fastlane):
- Traffic progression: 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> staggered region ramp
- Canary cohort size: min 50 qps or up to 10% of AZ capacity (whichever is smaller)
- Evaluation windows: 30m, 45m, 2h
- Key metrics + thresholds (trip causes immediate rollback):
  - 95th latency increase > 25% relative to baseline
  - Error rate (5xx) > 0.5% absolute or 3x baseline
  - KV cache hit rate drop > 5 percentage points
  - Retry-rate increase > 2x baseline
  - Quality eval delta > 1.0% on held prompt set
- Fallback policy: auto-fallback to previous model binary and routing policy if any threshold triggers.

ROLLBACK MATRIX (decision guide):
- Severity A: customer-facing latency spike or sustained errors -> immediate rollback to previous binary and full service restart for canary cohort. Notify execs and CS.
- Severity B: degraded metrics but partial service continuity (noncritical feature) -> pause rollout, scale canary down to 0, collect traces for 1h, escalate if unresolved.
- Severity C: cosmetic or low-sev regressions (UI/telemetry noise) -> document and continue with planned gradual ramp; schedule hotfix in next sprint.

OBSERVABILITY PLAY (dashboards & queries to watch):
- Dashboards: rollout/latency-trending, rollout/error-decomp, kv-cache-health, router-fallbacks, token-cost-sampler.
- Quick queries:
  - count_over_time(errors{env:prod,cohort:canary}[5m])
  - histogram_quantile(0.95, rate(latency_bucket[5m])) by (cohort)
  - sum(rate(kv_cache_hit_total[5m])) / sum(rate(kv_cache_req_total[5m]))
- Tracing: ensure sampled traces from canary cohort show proper KV cache path and no repeated retries loop.
- Synthetic checks: run the short prompt set at the start of each evaluation window and attach results to the runbook.

SURGE MITIGATION (fast actions):
- Throttle config: reduce non-essential background requests (telemetry/analytics) by 80% in canary cohort.
- Circuit breaker: trip on sustained queue depth > 50 for > 5m, divert traffic to fallback router.
- Autoscale: temporarily raise max-concurrency limit in dedicated pools by 20% to absorb transient spikes (only if latency stable).

SMOKE TESTS (day-of quick list):
- [ ] Endpoint health /ready and /live
- [ ] Representative generate and chat flows (streaming + non-streaming)
- [ ] Embedding endpoint consistency (spot-check 3 inputs)
- [ ] Billing/quotas sanity (ensure no unexpected billing spikes)

POST-DEPLOY (first 24h):
- T+6h: human check-in: SRE + runtime lead to validate metrics and decide final ramp or rollback.
- T+12h: CS alerting: notify small set of customers about change (if relevant).
- T+24h: add release notes to release-digest, attach PRs and key telemetry snapshots.
- T+72h: freeze release for formal postmortem window; if any incidents, open incident ticket and tag RINF-xxxx.

RELEASE NOTES DRAFT (to paste into release digest):
- Title: serving-runtime v2.11.3 - kv-cache fence and retry backoff tuning
- Summary: This micro-release improves KV cache fence handling to avoid stale read races and reduces excessive immediate retries by adding exponential backoff jitter. Expected impact: lower transient 5xxs under cache churn, slight improvement in tail latency for cold starts.
- Changes included:
  - runtime: kv-cache fence fix (PR 412)
  - runtime: retry backoff jitter added (PR 410)
  - infra: canary router gating config update (PR 419)
- Risk notes: Only affects hosted and dedicated flows; private deployments unchanged. Canary rollout plan executed. No customer-facing incidents observed during canary.
- Rollback instructions: revert to image tag serving-runtime:2.11.2 and reapply router policy; commands: kubectl set image ... (ops playbook refs).

KNOWN ISSUES / TODO (capture during run):
- Observed: sporadic cold-start spike at T+1h in eu-west-1 (investigating trace loops) -> assigned to Ethan (ticket RINF-2401).
- TODO: add an automated synthetic run at canary start to validate quality metric (owner: Priya).
- TODO: bake a small e2e that exercises kv-cache eviction during CI.

DEBRIEF TEMPLATE (fill immediately after rollout):
- Outcome: success/partial/rollback -> 
- What tripped thresholds? list metrics and timestamps -> 
- Actions taken (immediate + follow-up) -> 
- Owners assigned for fixes -> 
- Lessons & runbook updates (append below) -> 

NOTES TO SELF / QUICK REMINDERS:
- Keep the canary cohort pinned to a single AZ for predictable latency baseline.
- When muting alerts, leave business-critical alerting on. Document any mute windows in the incident channel.
- If rollback is performed, capture a full trace bundle for the 1h before rollback.
- After rollout, export the 95th percentile latency snapshots for 0%, 1%, 5%, 20% cohorts to the release artifact folder.

APPENDICES:
- Useful links: see linked_artifacts above.
- Contact rotation: on-call SRE (Lucas Rivera), runtime lead (Maya Thompson), infra on-call (Ethan Park).

END OF FASTLANE PLAYBOOK - copy this template for future micro-releases and update thresholds per feature area.
